source: US Core IG v6.1 DiagnosticReport (Note) profile; ONC (g)(10) §170.315(g)(10)(i)
description: App must construct a US Core-conformant DiagnosticReport (status, code, subject, result reference) and successfully POST it to Epic
remediation_hint: Ensure the DiagnosticReport includes status, category, code, subject reference, and a result reference to its Observation, and that the POST returns 2xx (not 401/403/422).

source: US Core IG v6.1 Observation profile; ONC (g)(10) §170.315(g)(10)(i)
description: App must construct a US Core-conformant Observation for the AI diagnosis finding and successfully POST it to Epic
remediation_hint: Ensure the Observation includes status, category, code, and a subject reference, and that the POST returns 2xx.

source: HL7 FHIR R4 Media resource (no US Core 3.1.1 profile exists for Media)
description: App must construct a valid Media resource referencing the source photo and successfully POST it to Epic
remediation_hint: Ensure the Media resource includes status, subject reference, and content (contentType + url or data), and that the POST returns 2xx.

source: SMART App Launch IG v2.0 §7 (scopes); ONC (g)(10) §170.315(g)(10)(v)(A)
description: Write scopes granted at launch (patient/DiagnosticReport.write, patient/Observation.write, patient/Media.write) must actually be honored, proven by successful writes rather than by inspecting the requested scope string
remediation_hint: Request patient/DiagnosticReport.write, patient/Observation.write, and patient/Media.write at launch and confirm Epic's app registration grants them — a 401/403 on any write means the scope was requested but not honored.
